Subject: Clarifications needed on Model provenance & license items (RFP section 4)

Hi Jonas / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are finishing up Section 4 of our RFP (Model Catalog & Licensing) and have a few follow-up clarifications from our legal and procurement teams to make sure there are no surprises during procurement. Please see short list below — numbered to match the RFP: 

1) For each model in your hosted catalog, do you provide explicit license metadata (license name + link) surfaced via the API and Console?
2) Can you confirm the provenance fields you store for models (origin URL, training data provenance summary, vendor/maintainer contact)?
3) Do you support version pinning per-tenant or per-route (i.e., freeze to model X.v2.1 for production)?
4) How do you handle models that have mixed licenses or downstream restrictions (e.g., non-commercial terms)?
5) What is your process and SLA for notifying customers of model updates or security-related patches?

We appreciate concise answers so we can include them verbatim in our procurement sheet. If easier, a short matrix or a single-page summary would be great.

Also attaching our prioritized scoring grid — if you can return by EOD Friday it would be very helpful.

Thanks,
Alice

Hi Alice — quick technical answers below. Will attach a compact matrix (license_matrix.xlsx) and a short catalog export.

1) License metadata: Yes. Each catalog entry in the Console and /models API includes a license_name field and license_url. We also surface a license_score (internal classification) in the Console for quick filtering.

2) Provenance fields: We store the following properties for each model: origin_url, originating_organization, training_data_summary (high-level), upstream_model_ids (list of immutable IDs), packaging_hash (sha256), and maintainer_contact. All are available in catalog export (CSV/JSON) and via the /models/{id} endpoint.

3) Version pinning: Supported. Customers can pin at three levels: tenant-default, project/route, and per-request override. Pinning creates an immutable binding to a model artifact id and KV cache snapshot; we persist the mapping in the customer control plane until explicitly changed. Rollback is supported via the Console.

4) Mixed licenses: Our catalog flags models that contain mixed-license components and surfaces a license_risk flag. For models with restrictive downstream terms (non-commercial, patent encumbrances), we mark them as restricted and exclude them from the default catalog for hosted tiers; they remain available for Dedicated/Private deployments with documented restrictions and required customer attestations.

5) Update notifications: We provide a change-log feed per model (audit entries with timestamp, author, and diff summary). For security or breaking changes we send immediate email notifications (SLA: 48 hours initial notice, 7-day remediation guidance). Customers can subscribe to automated update policies (notify-only, auto-approve minor patches, block-major-updates).

Attachments: license_matrix.xlsx (condensed mapping), Redwood_Model_Catalog_Provenance_Summary.pdf (one-page export)

Let me know if you want additional detail in any cell — happy to expand.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Product — Model Catalog
Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarifications needed on Model provenance & license items (RFP section 4)

Hi Alice / team — following up with legal language and contractual notes. High level responses suitable for insertion into your RFP procurement sheet: 

- License metadata & provenance: Redwood will provide, for each model, a canonical license identifier and a pointer (URL) to the license text. We will also include provenance metadata as noted by Laura. We recommend referencing the catalog export as the authoritative source of current license/provenance state.

- Model licensing policy: Redwood does not re-license third-party models. We restrict availability in hosted tiers when license terms impose downstream usage constraints; for Dedicated/Private customers, we provide the model artifact and license metadata but require customer confirmation of compliance with the upstream license.

- Version pinning & auditability: We confirm we can bind production routes to immutable model artifact IDs and that those bindings, along with who changed them and when, appear in audit logs that meet standard enterprise retention policies. This is suitable contractual language: "Redwood will: (i) allow customers to pin model versions to immutable artifact identifiers; (ii) retain change logs for pinned mappings for a minimum of 12 months; (iii) provide exportable audit evidence on request within 5 business days."

- Mixed-license handling & indemnity: Where a model includes components with restrictive downstream terms, Redwood will: (i) classify such models with a license_risk flag; (ii) surface required customer attestations; and (iii) exclude such models from certain hosted tiers unless explicitly enabled. We cannot indemnify customers for third-party license compliance beyond providing provenance and reasonable operational controls; any indemnity beyond that will need explicit negotiation and will be scoped in the contract.

- Update / security notifications: Redwood will notify customers via email and Console for security-relevant updates per the SLA listed in Section 5 of the standard Master Services Agreement.

Attached: RFI_Answers_20260621.docx (consolidated answers), suggested contract language snippet (pasted below).

Suggested snippet (editable):
"Customer may pin model routes to specific artifact identifiers. Redwood will maintain provenance metadata and license pointers for each artifact. Customer acknowledges responsibility for compliance with upstream license terms for artifacts obtained under third-party licenses; Redwood will provide evidence of provenance and reasonable operational controls but will not assume indemnity obligations for pre-existing third-party license restrictions unless explicitly agreed in writing."

If you want, we can provide a tracked-change version for your legal team to review.

Best,
Monica Patel
Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
